FILE: ./loudness_check.py — prove the finished program's audio is at a correct, safe master level.

CLI: loudness_check.py --final PATH [--target-lufs -16] [--tolerance-lu 1.5] [--max-true-peak-dbtp -1.0] [--json OUT]

Measure the final program (final/episode.mp4 or .mp3) with ffmpeg EBU R128: run `ffmpeg -i FINAL -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` (or loudnorm print_format=json in a first-pass measurement) and parse Integrated loudness (LUFS) and true peak (dBTP). Podcast target is -16 LUFS by default (named constant with rationale: the Apple/Spotify podcast norm), tolerance +/- a named LU constant. True peak must not exceed the max (default -1.0 dBTP, named constant) or the file is clipping / will be penalized by platforms. Report integrated LUFS, LRA if available, and true peak with pass/fail per limit and the WHY. A program at -30 LUFS (too quiet) or +0.5 dBTP (clipping) must FAIL. Exit 2 if the file has no audio stream or ffmpeg cannot measure it.

Add a small self-test path guarded by `if __name__` is not needed; the coordinator will red-prove it on real files. But your DETECT logic must be correct: do not confuse momentary/short-term with integrated loudness — the gate is on INTEGRATED loudness over the whole program.
tasks.check: python3 '/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/script_check.py' loudness_check.py argparse 'episode,fred' && (grep -qE 'sys.exit\(2\)|exit\(2\)|return 2' loudness_check.py || (echo 'FAIL: no exit-2 unusable-input path'; exit 1)) && echo 'PASS: instrument shape verified'
tasks.verified: a standalone deterministic master-loudness-check receipt; coordinator red-proves it on real media after the recut

FILE: ./blackframe_check.py — prove the finished video has no unintended black frames, flash frames, or freeze-gaps at edit points.

CLI: blackframe_check.py --render PATH [--boundaries PATH] [--max-black-s 0.10] [--json OUT]

Use ffmpeg blackdetect: `ffmpeg -i RENDER -vf blackdetect=d=0.05:pix_th=0.10 -an -f null -` and parse the black_start/black_end/black_duration lines from stderr. Any black span longer than --max-black-s (named constant, default 0.10s = ~3 frames at 30fps; a legitimate fade-to-black intro/outro is allowed ONLY in the first/last N seconds — make that a named constant, e.g. FADE_GRACE_S=3.0, and exempt black within it). A black span in the BODY of the program is a flash-frame / render-drop defect and must FAIL, reporting each offending span's start and duration. If --boundaries (the angle_switched .boundaries.json sidecar) is given, additionally flag any black span that lands within a small window of an edit boundary as an edit-point flash, which is the highest-value catch. Exit 2 if the render has no video stream.

Do NOT fail on a single sub-threshold black frame from encoding; the threshold exists to separate real gaps from codec noise. State the threshold rationale in a comment.
